title: The star formation region NGC 6559
caption: The star-forming region NGC 6559, imaged by the Danish 1.54-meter telescope at La Silla

recognition.text: Official ESO press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: Red clouds, blue patches and dark regions jostle together in this image of NGC 6559, a place where stars are forming inside an interstellar cloud. It was taken with the Danish 1.54-meter telescope at ESO's La Silla Observatory in Chile.

Each color tells of a different process. The red clouds are made mostly of hydrogen gas, which glows when it is energized. The blue areas are where starlight bounces off tiny particles of dust, much as sunlight scatters in Earth's sky. The dark regions are places where dust is so thick that it becomes opaque and blocks the light behind it.
ESO describes the scene as showing the anarchy that reigns when stars form, with glowing gas, reflecting dust and dark clouds tangled together in one patch of sky.

understand.summary: The DFOSC instrument on the Danish 1.54-meter telescope took this visible-light image through B, V, R and hydrogen-alpha filters. The color mapping isn't published.
understand.eye: The camera's long exposures reveal faint colored clouds that the eye could not see.
